source: A game where start at a stop with a train rail and every while or so there is a building with a gun inside. It has a 60 percent change of being a 1890s sawed off double barrel shotgun, 30 percent change of being a 1890s rifle, and a 10 pent chance of a 1890s bolt action rifle. There is a train that comes by every minute or so and you can hop on it. Some times you see a big green zombie. You can shoot it to hurt it and kill it.

answers.ask: How far does the rail run - a handful of buildings, or a line long enough that the train ride matters?
answers.answer: Make it a short line with a handful of buildings along it, so it stays small and playable.

answers.ask: Is there an end to the line, or is it an endless ride with zombies along the way?
answers.answer: Use an endless ride with zombies appearing along the way; the prompt does not call for an ending.

config.genre_evidence: “an endless ride with zombies appearing along the way” makes the space an ongoing threat-survival route. Guns in buildings and the ability to “shoot [zombies] to hurt it and kill it” add Shooter mechanics, but the layout is built around enduring recurring zombie threats on the rail line rather than firing corridors or a competitive deathmatch.

config.addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this Survival map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Contained Arena: A clearly bounded space the round plays out in, keeping the threat and the player in meaningful proximity.

INCLUDE:
- Crawlspaces & Lockers: Small localized cutouts built into lower walls where players break enemy sightlines and hide. Minimum 4 studs on the entry axis (Part I §2).
- Enterable Shelter: Buildings players flee into and hide inside.
